subject: Streaming probe alignment — measurement slate & next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Park <lauren@quickcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming probe alignment — measurement slate & next steps

Thanks for the sync earlier, Lauren — quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope the qualification run. Great conversation; I captured the high-level targets and what we need from your side to make the benchmark reproducible on both sides.

Summary of customer targets (from call)
- Latency goal: p95 <= 200ms for interactive streaming responses (end-to-end from request to first chunk delivery).
- Sustained throughput: ~10 QPS (in-region) with burst tolerance up to 75 concurrent streams during peak sale events.
- Average response length: ~120 tokens (range 30–450).
- Streaming behavior: client expects chunked frames approximately every 15–30 tokens; ability to disable batch-aggregation for low-latency traffic is critical.

What we propose to validate (Redwood measurement slate v1)
- Measurement axes: p50/p95/p99 for first-chunk latency, total-latency to final token, and per-chunk inter-arrival consistency.
- Workload model: replay of recorded production traces (sample attached) + synthetic prompt mixes.
- Concurrency experiments: steady-state runs at 1/5/10/25 QPS and spike runs that ramp to 75–80 concurrent streams for 10 minutes.
- Repro rules: 5 independent repeats, clear seed for prompt RNG, KV-cache ON/OFF runs, and quantization parity checks.

Immediate asks from QuickCommerce (what we need)
1) Sample prompt set used in discovery (attach CSV) — please include representative user-system pairs and average token counts.
2) A staging API endpoint or short-lived test token so our harness can replay traces from your staging VPC (if you prefer, we can bring our runner into your VPC).
3) Confirmation of model variant(s) to pin for the run (e.g., LlamaX-13b-fp16 / quantized variants).
4) Preferred window to run the benchmark (we propose Wed 9/20 or Thu 9/21 morning PT).

I've attached measurement_slate_v1.xlsx (detailed matrix) and a starter sample_prompts_streaming.csv. Ben / Marissa — can you review the reproducibility checklist (runbook_checks.md) and confirm whether the proposed repeats & KV toggles are reasonable?

Next steps
- Lauren: share the confirmed prompt set + staging access (or let us know if staging-run-in-your-VPC is required).
- QuickCommerce procurement: we expect a short SOW for the dedicated benchmark window if Redwood runs against QuickCommerce staging.
- Redwood: we'll prep the harness and share a run plan 48 hours before the agreed date.

Thanks — Steph

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

[Attachment: sample_prompts_streaming.csv (csv)]

From: Lauren Park <lauren@quickcommerce.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops-eng@quickcommerce.com, procurement@quickcommerce.com
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 14:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming probe alignment — measurement slate & next steps

Thanks, Stephanie — this lines up with what we discussed. I'm attaching a cleaned version of the prompt set (same format as the CSV you included) and a small sample trace export so you can see burst characteristics.

Few clarifications:
- Peak concurrency: we see short peaks (10-minute windows) up to ~80 concurrent live streams during flash promotions — sustained concurrency is ~8–12.
- Token patterns: most responses are short (~40–80 tokens), but 5–10% of queries produce long outputs (200–450 tokens) — we need the SLOs to hold across that skew.
- Streaming cadence: our client-side chunking requests frames roughly every 20 tokens; if Redwood's runtime batches at larger token windows it increases first-byte latency in our app.

We can provide a staging API key scoped to a sandbox dataset and a staging host (staging.quickcommerce-internal.net). We prefer Redwood to run the harness from your side initially. If anything will touch PII in traces we'll scrub before you get it.

Attaching: sample_prompts_streaming.csv (your starter + our augmentations), production_trace_sample.json (sanitized), and a link to our internal perf dashboard.

I'll loop procurement to start the simple SOW for the benchmark engagement. Proposed run dates are fine — prefer 9/20 morning PT.

Cheers,
Lauren
Head of Platform, QuickCommerce
lauren@quickcommerce.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Park <lauren@quickcommerce.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming probe alignment — measurement slate & next steps

Appreciate the artifacts, Lauren. A couple of methodological notes from our side to keep the results rigorous and reproducible: 

1) Measurement definitions (we'll include in the XLS):
   - First-chunk latency: time from request-in to first stream chunk emitted by the model (client sees first token).
   - Final-token latency: time from request-in to stream close + last-token visibility.
   - Inter-chunk jitter: standard deviation of the per-chunk intervals across a response.

2) Run configuration we will execute (read-only staging):
   - Pin model to LlamaX-13b-fp16 and run quantized parity: native fp16 vs int8-qat where supported.
   - Cache experiments: (A) cold-run (KV disabled), (B) warm-run (KV enabled, with 10k-entry prefix warmup).
   - Repeats: 5 independent repeats per experiment; compute median and 95% CI.
   - Traffic replay: we will ingest sanitized production_trace_sample.json and replay timings to match burst windows.

3) Repro checklist (quick):
   - Seeded RNG in harness (we'll publish seeds in run artifacts).
   - Exact prompt bundle (we'll store the CSV versioned).
   - Runtime flags (batching window, chunk flush threshold) exported with results.

Operational question: to avoid network variance, would QuickCommerce consider a short VPC peering or temporary tunnel for the benchmark window? If not, our plan B is to run from Redwood-hosted infra against staging host at staging.quickcommerce-internal.net and include network tail as part of measurement.

Procurement note: Ben, when QuickCommerce confirms SOW we should include clause for a 2-4 hour quiet window to run the peak spike tests.

Lauren — if you confirm the staging key + preferred run window (9/20 9:00–12:00 PT), we'll lock the plan and send a run schedule + expected artifacts 48 hours prior. Attaching runbook_checks.md with the items we'll collect.

Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Performance | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

[Attachment: runbook_checks.md (md)]
